name: Dylan

attributes.attribute: stepped over Math's wand and dropped a baby
son of the wave, son of the sea
swam like a fish and loved the waves

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dylan was a Welsh hero or god. He carried the names Dylan Son-of-Wave and Dylan Eil Ton. Arianrhod wanted to be the ceremonial footholder to King Math of Wales. She stepped over Math's wand as a test. A baby fell from her womb. She did not know she was pregnant. The baby fled at once to the sea. People called him Dylan Ail Ton, son of the wave. They also called him Ail Mor, son of the sea. He was Arianrhod's child by a sea god or a merman. His other child that day was Lleu Lamb. The sea was Dylan's element. He swam like a fish. He enjoyed feeling the waves under his body. His uncle Gilfaethwy killed him. Gilfaethwy had raped Math's earlier footholder. That act set the whole story in motion.

okr.objective: Record Dylan as a Welsh son of the sea who died at the hand of his uncle.
key_results: Relate Dylan's birth when Arianrhod stepped over Math's wand
Define Dylan Ail Ton and Ail Mor as son of the wave and son of the sea
State that his uncle Gilfaethwy killed the sea-child Dylan
